lacuna.repo_anchor: research/lacunae/outline.yaml, ecosystem-strategy item triton-fma-floor-sm75: 'possibly the load-bearing constraint: ... MXFP4 emulation requires Triton >=3.4 while Turing tensor-core health requires <=3.2 - a dependency deadlock. Which kernels, version pins, or patches escape it, and what a CUDA-native substitute strategy looks like.' The constraint is recorded twice in the plans and assumed in five sibling result rows. plan/0006-cu-sm80-on-sm75/README.md (roadmap surroundings): 'served by FLA Triton on sm_75, but Triton's tl.dot lost tensor cores below sm80 in Triton 3.3'. plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md execution record: 'Triton's tl.dot falls back to FMA below sm_80, so chunked prefill there is FMA-bound - an sm_75 GDN microbench is its own future item, not built here.' Siblings defer their shared decision to this item: gdn-linear-attention-sm75.json ('the Triton-pin A/B (3.2 m16n8k8 vs >=3.4 FMA) ... the single highest-information cheap experiment'), moe-kernels-sm75.json ('the sweep is only meaningful after the Triton-pin decision (cross-item triton-fma-floor-sm75), so sequence pin-then-tune'), mxfp4-nvfp4-ecosystem.json ('the lane pin triton <= 3.2 keeps MMAv2 m16n8k8 tensor cores but conflicts with triton_kernels >= 3.4'), and turing-engine-upstream-drift.json (a 'known-good Triton pin decision (<=3.2 or a >=3.4 verified on sm75) recorded in environment.md' still listed as open work). NOTE: the sibling records conflict on lane state - mla/mxfp4 items assert 'the lane pins triton <=3.2' while the drift item lists the pin as undecided; settling that inconsistency is part of this item [uncertain: actual triton version installed in the lane venv, not re-verified here].
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the FMA floor is confirmed as deliberate upstream policy, the escape routes are all identified and each has a measured or metadata-verified basis. (1) The codegen event line, source-verified: triton PR #5066 ('[BACKEND] Deprecate MMAv1; fallback to FMA for computeCapability < 80', merged 2024-11-05) shipped in triton 3.3.0 (PyPI 2025-04-09); restore attempt PR #9970 ('[BACKEND] Restore MMA support for Turing GPUs', opened 2026-04-08 by nlzy, closed next day by ThomasRaoux) argued 'Turing uses the MMAv2 layout, so PR #5066 inadvertently killed Turing', re-admitted cc75 in AccelerateMatmul.cpp plus test fixes in one commit, and moved test_core.py from 107 to 54 failures - still broken. Declined with: 'We don't want to officially support Turing. We can do best effort support for non invasive feature but not more' (ThomasRaoux), 'we don't have any CI machines with sm75 and cannot guarantee correctness going forward' (Jokeren), who also offered 'Either we have a dedicated person maintaining the Turing path' or Turing CI hardware as the only acceptable paths - both rejected. The correction carried from this run's GDN item holds: at tag v3.2.0, getMMAVersionSafe maps cc 75-89 to MMAv2 and MMAv2.cpp emits Turing-native mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k8 (f32-acc and f16-acc variants), so 3.2.0 (PyPI 2025-01-22) is the last MMA-bearing Triton for sm75 and the 3.2 pin is a real tensor-core-recovery lever. The 2021 era (#189, still open) was the mma.884 half-rate problem; the current era is no-MMA-at-all. (2) Release ladder (PyPI): 3.2.0 2025-01-22; 3.3.0 2025-04-09 (FMA floor + the #6698 f16-conversion LLVM crash on cc<8.0, fixed by #7585 merged 2025-07-22, carried from 3.4); 3.3.1 2025-05-29; 3.4.0 2025-07-30 (tl.dot_scaled/mxfp4-reliable: HF transformers quantizer_mxfp4 gates 'CUDA requires Triton >= 3.4.0' + triton_kernels installed, else 'default to dequantizing the model to bf16'; tl.dot_scaled itself shipped in 3.3, with the DecomposeScaledBlocked emulation pass for non-Blackwell GPUs, per triton #7550); 3.5.0 2025-10-13; 3.6.0 (torch 2.11.0 pins it; introduced an unlisted breaking rhs_scale shape change in tl.dot_scaled, triton #10007); 3.7.1 (torch 2.13.0 pin); 3.8.0 current on PyPI (triton-windows already tracks 3.8 / PyTorch 2.14). (3) The coupling mechanism - triton is NOT pinned by vLLM but by torch wheel metadata (verified via PyPI requires_dist): torch 2.6.0 (2025-01-29) -> triton==3.2.0 (Linux x86_64); 2.7.1 (2025-06-04) -> 3.3.1; 2.8.0 (2025-08-06) -> 3.4.0; 2.11.0 (2026-03-23) -> 3.6.0; 2.13.0 (2026-07-08) -> 3.7.1. Inductor emits version-paired Triton, so downgrading triton under a newer torch breaks torch.compile (community evidence class: ComfyUI-GGUF #311, pytorch 2.7.1 + triton 3.2) - the pin drags torch with it, and torch drags vLLM. (4) vLLM carrier mapping (verified at tags): v0.8.5 -> torch==2.6.0 -> triton 3.2.0 (the last stock vLLM on 3.2, confirming the brief's 'v0.8.x torch 2.6 natural carrier'); v0.9.0 -> torch 2.7.0 -> 3.3.0; v0.10.0 -> torch 2.7.1 -> 3.3.1; v0.21.0 -> torch 2.11.0 -> 3.6.0 (the weicj fork base); v0.28.0 (2026-08-26, current) -> torch==2.13.0 -> triton 3.7.1 - five minor lines past the last MMA-bearing release; v0.28.0 pins neither triton nor triton_kernels directly. (5) Consumer-stack floors: current flash-linear-attention (0.5.x line) requires triton>=3.3 AND torch>=2.7.0 in its cuda extra (pyproject, verified), while fla 0.4.2 (2026-03-12, the community's last-good pin after the #792 NaN regression) declares no triton constraint at all - the 0.4.2 pin is simultaneously the last-good-pre-regression AND the last triton-3.2-compatible FLA, a coincidence that makes the 3.2 stack coherent; MXFP4 hard-requires >=3.4 + triton_kernels (transformers gate, LlamaFactory #8995 warning text). (6) The community Turing-MMA ecosystem answered #9970's closure: Chennesxu/triton-turing (MIT, referenced from #9970 via its issue #21) is ACTIVE with commits through 2026-09-06 and carries far more than the declined PR: the first cp.async-free software pipeliner for Turing (upstream pipelining assumes the Ampere-only cp.async), Turing autotune configs for the 64 KiB smem cap, fp16 m16n8k8 + INT8 m8n8k16 + INT4 m8n8k32 MMA paths (INT4 marked 'Not implemented' upstream), FA2 forward+backward, opt-in bf16-as-f16 dot (TRITON_SM75_BF16_DOT_AS_F16=1), fp8 e4m3 conversion below sm89, and an optional vendored triton_kernels install (pip install -e python/triton_kernels) - i.e. exactly the 'MMAv2 + dot_scaled both' fork the deadlock implies; its base upstream version is not stated [uncertain]. Benchmarks on Titan RTX: FA2 fwd +21-26% vs a hand-written CUDA/CUTLASS kernel at d=64 (+4-8% at d=128; bwd LOSES 13-16% at d=128 to smem-forced halved blocks), INT8 Triton ~1.8x cuBLAS INT8, INT4 peak 219 TOPS, FP16 GEMM 84-86% of cuBLAS, and bf16 dot 12.4x/17.7x/13.1x faster than the FMA fallback at 1024^3/2048^3/4096^3 - the only published FMA-vs-MMA Triton delta on sm75 silicon. triton-windows (Windows wheel line, now at Triton 3.8) confirms the floor in its GPU table: Turing 'Yes in Triton 3.2', 'Support for Volta and Turing was dropped since Triton 3.3, see triton-lang#5066', with issue #28 as the 'help maintain Turing in the latest Triton' coordination point; SageAttention issue #102 (a Turing user asking for Turing support above triton 3.2) closed without resolution - demand exists, no mainstream carrier does. (7) The one production-grade escape already proven: weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (base vLLM 0.21.0 + torch 2.11.0+cu128, i.e. triton 3.6 FMA) simply stops using Triton for anything compute-bound - fast prefill is FlashQLA/FlashInfer (CUDA), weights are Marlin (FP8/INT4/NVFP4 routes), GDN prefill is its own legacy CUDA kernel - Triton survives only where FMA is harmless. TileLang is the second Triton-class substrate that kept sm75: v0.1.9 (2026-04-22) fixed T.gemm on SM75, v0.1.10 native SM75 MMA GEMM (FP16/INT8/INT4), v0.1.12 f16-acc/UINT8 dispatchers, v0.1.13 FMA-fallback extension, v0.1.14 2026-09-02 latest.
lacuna.sm75_viability: The constraint, quantified: at the host's locked 1455 MHz the TU102 fp16 FMA ceiling is ~12.7 TFLOP/s (house arithmetic estimate) against the bridge kernel's measured 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s (m16n8k8, fp32-acc) and the incumbent Marlin's 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 - and triton-turing independently measured bf16 dot at 12.4-17.7x FMA speed on Titan RTX; FMA-only tl.dot is roughly an order of magnitude off tensor-core Triton, not a modest penalty. THE ESCAPE MATRIX (the item's ask): (A) VERSION-PIN STACK - vLLM v0.8.5 + torch 2.6.0 + triton 3.2.0 + fla 0.4.2, all metadata-verified coherent: every Triton dot (TRITON_ATTN prefill QK^T/PA, FLA chunked GDN, fused-MoE, any plain tl.dot GEMM) lowers to m16n8k8 with fp32 or fp16 accumulate. What breaks under the pin, concretely: (i) everything upstream after 2025-05 is absent - no Marlin-Turing (vLLM #29901, Dec 2025), no FlashInfer-on-sm75 (v0.11.1+ era), no TRITON_MLA backend, no MXFP4 (>=3.4 gate), no 2025-2026 model corpus - and critically the GDN hybrids that motivate the pin (Qwen3-Next-class, vLLM support from the 2025-09-11 launch) postdate v0.8.x, so the carrier cannot serve them without model-code backport [uncertain: exact first vLLM release carrying qwen3_next]; (ii) current FLA (>=0.5) refuses to install (triton>=3.3 floor) - fla 0.4.2 is the paired pin, which is also its post-#792 last-good, so no loss there; (iii) torch.compile on torch >=2.7 with triton 3.2 is broken-by-construction (Inductor emits version-paired Triton; wheel metadata conflicts) - the pin cannot be lifted onto newer vLLM by force-pip, it must take the whole v0.8.x era with it [uncertain: exact Inductor failure mode, documented via community reports not upstream statements]; (iv) the 3.3.0-3.3.1 crash window (#6698) is avoided entirely - the 3.2 pin is also the crash-free pin. (B) FORCE-NEW-TRITON, ACCEPT FMA - the weicj posture (torch 2.11/triton 3.6): viable only if every compute-bound Triton surface is substituted (see D); Triton then serves memory-bound non-dot kernels (MoE align/routing, quantization, sampling) where FMA vs MMA is irrelevant. (C) LOCAL PATCH TO CURRENT TRITON - the minimal MMAv2-restore is genuinely small (per #9970: re-admit cc75 in AccelerateMatmul.cpp + test fixes, single commit, MMAv2.cpp remains in-tree for Ampere) but #9970's own numbers show it buys 54 still-failing core tests, because upstream passes assume cc>=80 features - chiefly cp.async-based pipelining (Ampere-only instruction) and smem budgets above Turing's 64 KiB/CTA; the healthy patch set is triton-turing (no-cp.async pipeliner, Turing autotune configs, INT8/INT4 MMA, fp8-cvt below sm89, FA2), active 2026-09-06, MIT, source-install only - adopting it means owning a compiler fork against a codebase that officially refused the maintenance (rebase cost grows as backend passes refactor through 3.5-3.8); its optional vendored triton_kernels suggests the both-features fork (MMAv2 + dot_scaled) is being assembled, which would break the MXFP4 half of the deadlock too [uncertain: base version and dot_scaled-on-sm75 status in the fork]. (D) CUDA-NATIVE SUBSTITUTION (proven at production grade by weicj on 2080 Ti; the fork's own lane): attention via the FA2-sm75 quilt / the bridge kernel / FlashInfer 0.6.12 sm75 wheels; GEMM/MoE via Marlin-Turing (51-57 TFLOP/s house-measured), CUTLASS sm75 (mma_sm75.h), cuBLAS, the humming-kernel line; GDN via the weicj legacy CUDA forward (2.1x GDN-stage on 2080 Ti); MXFP4 via CUDA nibble dequant + Marlin W4A16 - never tl.dot_scaled. Every CUDA kernel is Triton-version-independent: this route escapes the deadlock by construction rather than resolving it. (E) SECOND SUBSTRATE - TileLang kept sm75 MMA (v0.1.9-v0.1.14, native FP16/INT8/INT4 GEMM): a Triton-class authoring stack where Turing tensor cores still work upstream-maintained; usable for new kernels, not for the existing Triton kernel corpus (FLA/vLLM kernels are Triton source). Attention-backend candidate matrix gate (sm75): TRITON_ATTN runs on any triton but prefill dots are FMA-slow on >=3.3 (decode partly bandwidth-bound, less affected); FLEX_ATTENTION inherits the same floor PLUS the torch-Inductor pairing constraint (cannot even hold triton 3.2 under torch >=2.7); TRITON_MLA nominally any-CC, unmeasured on sm75, needs the pin decision first; all CUDA backends (BRIDGE_ATTN, FA2-sm75 quilt, FLASHINFER 0.6.12-era, Marlin) unaffected by triton version entirely. Fallback semantics: the FMA-vs-MMA change is instruction selection, invisible at the API - there is NO error and NO silent dtype fallback, only a silent order-of-magnitude perf loss detectable solely by PTX/SASS inspection (grep mma.sync vs ffma), and a numerics shift at accumulation-order scale (fp32-acc FMA chains vs MMA k8 groups); autotuners additionally pick different winners per lowering (Turing's 64 KiB smem vs Ampere-tuned configs -> OutOfResources or bad configs, the #38918 class).

effort_value.effort_estimate: The item as scoped is a decision plus a probe, not a campaign: (1) the escape-matrix A/B in side venvs - current lane pin vs triton==3.2.0 + torch==2.6.0 (v0.8.5-class stack or standalone FLA 0.4.2) vs triton-turing built from source - over the existing oracle/ladder harness, with PTX/SASS mma-grep as the deterministic evidence and median-of-N timing only after numerics: 1-2 sessions; (2) the ledger row itself (pin/carrier breaks, patch scope and residual failures, substitution coverage) recorded in environment.md and the drift row: hours. Two follow-on sizes, owned by this item's verdict: adopting triton-turing as the lane's Triton = a compiler build lane plus a per-rebase regression ritual (medium, permanent tax - budget like a small CI system, and CUDA 13.3 toolchain compatibility is untested [uncertain]); backporting the GDN hybrid model code onto the v0.8.5 carrier = weeks and NOT recommended (the fork already carries a healthy sm75 engine - the pin would be for FLA kernels, backportable independently of the old vLLM). The CUDA-substitution completion rows (GDN microbench, MoE tuning) are sibling items and proceed under either verdict.
effort_value.unlocks: This is the shared dependency of five sibling rows: the GDN microbench's Triton-pin A/B leg, the fused-MoE config tuning sweep ('pin-then-tune' - meaningless until the codegen question is settled), the MXFP4 vehicle choice (tl.dot_scaled vs CUDA nibble dequant, structurally decided here), the TRITON_MLA measurement environment, and the FLEX_ATTENTION/torch.compile posture on sm75. A 'pin works' verdict unlocks tensor-core Triton prefill for the 27B hybrid's 75-percent GDN layer stack and for fused-MoE W4A16 dots at zero kernel-writing cost; a 'fork works' verdict additionally unlocks both sides of the deadlock at once (MMAv2 + dot_scaled via triton-turing's vendored triton_kernels, if it holds [uncertain]); a negative verdict formally retires Triton for compute on this host and ratifies the CUDA-native doctrine (bridge kernel, Marlin, legacy GDN, FA2-sm75 quilt), which frees every downstream item from Triton-version coupling permanently. For the operator's serving target specifically: it converts the FMA-bound GDN prefill that every recorded 27B engine number silently bundles into either a measured-and-accepted cost or a recovered tensor-core path.
effort_value.dependency_order: Nothing internal blocks the probe: the oracle harness, ladder, gpu-lease discipline, and the lane venv all exist, and side venvs are self-contained. It should land FIRST among the dependent rows (GDN microbench explicitly stages its Triton A/B as the highest-information leg; MoE tuning sequences after it). External prerequisites are only artifacts: triton 3.2.0/3.3.x wheels and torch 2.6.0 wheels from PyPI (frozen, always available), fla 0.4.2 from PyPI, and a triton-turing source build (needs a compiler toolchain lane; CUDA 13.3 compatibility unverified [uncertain] - falls back to the CUDA 12.x container if 13.3 chokes). Parallelizable from day one: the CUDA-substitution rows (bridge/Marlin are landed; GDN legacy-kernel build, MoE Marlin routing) run under either verdict - that is their advantage. Sequence inside the probe: venv construction -> numerics gate (fp64 oracle, finiteness asserts) -> PTX/SASS mma-grep -> timing ladder -> ledger row -> verdict propagated to environment.md and the sibling items.
effort_value.risk_notes: Correctness/numerics: (1) FMA vs MMA lowerings differ in accumulation grouping - comparisons across triton versions are statistical (fp16-roundoff band), never bitwise; the fp64-oracle gate must run per-pin, not be inherited; (2) the full-rate path on Turing MMA is fp16-accumulate (fp32-acc halves tensor-core throughput, the Marlin-Turing house finding) - any move to f16-acc tl.dot for speed is a real numerics downgrade needing magnitude-regression gates; (3) #9970 left 54/6182 core tests failing with the minimal restore - a locally patched Triton is correctness-unproven for arbitrary kernels, and Triton's failure mode on this host's history is silent-wrong, not loud; (4) FLA's exp-of-cumsum NaN class (#792) is instruction-selection-independent and rides along under any pin - finiteness asserts are mandatory before timing. Upstream-drift exposure: severe and asymmetric - the 3.2 pin is frozen forever (a 2025-01 compiler; no fixes, python/CUDA wheel-window risk [uncertain]), while triton-turing is a 43-star effectively-single-maintainer fork against a codebase whose maintainers formally declined Turing CI or a dedicated maintainer (#9970) - every upstream rebase re-touches backend passes, and even Triton's own API churns under consumers (#10007's unlisted dot_scaled break); the weicj forks (same ecosystem) went 10-star-dark-adjacent before. Silent-perf cliffs are the dominant operational hazard: the FMA fallback never errors, autotuners pick different winners per lowering, and Turing's 64 KiB smem turns Ampere-tuned configs into OutOfResources or bad choices (#38918 class) - only a PTX/SASS assertion (mma.sync present) plus frozen tuned configs catch these. The records-level inconsistency (sibling items assert a lane triton<=3.2 pin that the drift item lists as undecided) must be resolved empirically in the probe or every downstream 'pin' claim inherits it.
effort_value.determinism_class: Statistical across lowerings, bitwise-stable within one: a Triton kernel at a fixed (version, config, shape) is deterministic - FMA and m16n8k8 paths each have fixed reduction orders - but the same kernel under different triton versions or FMA-vs-MMA selection moves results at fp16-roundoff scale via different accumulation grouping; cross-pin comparisons are band-checked, never bitwise. Run-to-run and restart-to-restart variance enters through Triton autotune (time-based config selection, cache-persistence across restarts) - configs must be pinned or logged per transcript, the same discipline the MoE row adopts (frozen tuned configs, no serve-time autotune). The deterministic, oracle-checkable evidence unique to this item is the codegen assertion itself: PTX/SASS inspection for mma.sync.m16n8k8 vs ffma is a build-level check that does not vary run-to-run and should be a standing gate next to the numerics oracle - stronger than any timing evidence. Patched-compiler caveat: triton-turing's no-cp.async pipeliner is a new scheduling pass; treat each fork rebuild as a new numeric entity requiring an oracle re-run rather than inherited attestation (scheduling-dependent fp reordering is not expected but unproven). float64-oracle + median-of-N discipline maps directly: oracle per (pin, config), finiteness asserts before timing, medians for throughput, PTX evidence version-stamped in the ledger.

decision.priority_signal: FOR doing this next: it is the named load-bearing constraint of the ecosystem-strategy sweep - five sibling rows (GDN, MoE, MXFP4, MLA, engine-drift) explicitly defer their Triton decision to it, so its 1-2-session probe unblocks more items per hour than anything else open; the escape evidence is now complete enough to decide (wheel-metadata-verified pin ladder, a declined-but-diffed restore PR, an active community fork with published sm75 benchmarks, and a production fork proving CUDA substitution); triton-turing is healthy TODAY (commits 2026-09-06) but is exactly the kind of 43-star single-maintainer artifact that disappears - the #9970 author's threatened personal-fork path is what it IS; and the house records currently contradict themselves on whether the lane already pins 3.2, an inconsistency that taints every downstream claim until settled. AGAINST: the CUDA-native answers for the big surfaces are already landed in-fork (bridge attention 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s, Marlin 51-57), so Triton tensor cores matter chiefly for FLA GDN chunked prefill and fused-MoE - both with pin-free alternatives (weicj legacy GDN kernel, Marlin MoE); the v0.8.5 carrier is a dead end for model coverage (cannot even serve the GDN hybrids that motivate it) so the pin route's value is FLA-kernel-shaped, not engine-shaped; and a compiler fork is a permanent tax with upstream on record refusing to help. Net: high-priority-but-cheap - run the probe now, decide adopt-patch vs CUDA-only-doctrine on the measured GDN/MoE delta (adopt triton-turing only if tensor-core Triton beats the substitution roadmap materially on those two surfaces), and record the verdict as the standing environment.md row the drift item already calls for.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 probe, oracle-first, no timing until numerics are green, 1-2 sessions of card time on the TU102 host under the standing lease/median discipline: (1) three side venvs - (a) the lane's current triton (first, record what it actually is - this settles the sibling-records contradiction), (b) triton==3.2.0 with torch==2.6.0 + fla 0.4.2 (standalone FLA is sufficient; a v0.8.5 vLLM install is optional confirmation), (c) triton-turing built from source (CUDA 12.x container if 13.3 fails); (2) numerics gate: FLA 0.4.2 chunk_gated_delta_rule at the 27B shapes with T%64!=0 tail cases and gate-magnitude sweeps plus a plain tl.dot fp16 GEMM and (where installable) the vLLM fused-MoE kernel, differential against fp64 torch references with all-finite asserts (#792 tripwire) - accept cross-venv diffs at fp16-band scale, disqualify any NaN/garbage; (3) the deterministic evidence: dump PTX/SASS per venv, grep for mma.sync.m16n8k8 vs ffma, version-stamp the result - this is the load-bearing artifact; (4) only then timing, median-of-5, locked 1455 MHz: GDN chunk ms/token, fused-MoE M512, dense tl.dot GEMM as the FMA-vs-MMA ratio row (expect the triton-turing-class 12-18x delta on bf16 dots if MMA is live; anything >=3x on the GEMM row decides the pin question); (5) optional same-day leg: triton-turing's FA2 and INT8/INT4 tutorials on the same card to size the fork's total value. Deliverable: the escape-matrix ledger row (venv-A/B/C codegen evidence + numerics transcripts + timing table + explicit pin/carrier/fork/substitution verdicts) written to environment.md and referenced from the GDN, MoE, MXFP4, MLA and drift rows - the single artifact that retires the deadlock as this sweep's shared unknown.

We can do best effort support for non invasive feature but not more' / 'we don't have any CI machines with sm75'; references SageAttention #102, triton-windows #28, Chennesxu/triton-turing #21): https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/9970

triton-lang/triton v3.2.0 source (source-verified in this run's GDN item): lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/AccelerateMatmul.cpp getMMAVersionSafe (cc 75-89 -> MMAv2) and third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/DotOpToLLVM/MMAv2.cpp (mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k8 .f32.f16.f16.f32 and .f16.f16.f16.f16) - the <=3.2 Turing tensor-core path: https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/tree/v3.2.0

vLLM requirements at release tags (verified 2026-09-07): v0.8.5 torch==2.6.0 (the last stock vLLM on triton 3.2); v0.9.0 torch==2.7.0; v0.10.0 torch==2.7.1; v0.21.0 torch==2.11.0; v0.28.0 torch==2.13.0, no direct triton or triton_kernels pin: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/v0.8.5/requirements/cuda.txt et al.

fla-org/flash-linear-attention pyproject.toml - main requires triton>=3.3 and torch>=2.7.0 (cuda extra); tag v0.4.2 declares no triton constraint (works on 3.2; also the post-#792 last-good pin): https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/main/pyproject.toml and https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/v0.4.2/pyproject.toml

HuggingFace transformers MXFP4 gate 'CUDA requires Triton >= 3.4.0' (quantizer_mxfp4) and the ecosystem warning 'MXFP4 quantization requires triton >= 3.4.0 and triton_kernels installed, we will default to dequantizing the model to bf16' (LlamaFactory #8995, gpt-oss threads): https://github.com/hiyouga/LlamaFactory/issues/8995

triton issue #7550 (tl.dot_scaled uses fp16/bf16 MMA via DecomposeScaledBlocked on GPUs without native block-scaled support) and issue #10007 (Triton 3.6.0 breaking rhs_scale shape change in tl.dot_scaled, unlisted in release notes): https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/7550 and https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/10007

Chennesxu/triton-turing (community Turing-MMA Triton fork, active through 2026-09-06; cp.async-free Turing pipelining, 64 KiB-smem autotunes, FP16 m16n8k8 / INT8 m8n8k16 / INT4 m8n8k32 MMA, FA2 fwd+bwd, TRITON_SM75_BF16_DOT_AS_F16, fp8 e4m3 cvt below sm89, optional vendored triton_kernels; Titan RTX benchmarks: FA2 fwd +21-26% vs hand CUDA at d=64, INT8 ~1.8x cuBLAS, FP16 GEMM 84-86% of cuBLAS, bf16 dot 12.4x/17.7x/13.1x vs FMA fallback at 1024^3/2048^3/4096^3; base upstream version unstated): https://github.com/Chennesxu/triton-turing

triton-lang/triton-windows README (GPU support table: Turing 'Yes in Triton 3.2', 'Support for Volta and Turing was dropped since Triton 3.3, see triton-lang#5066'; issue #28 coordinates Turing maintenance in latest Triton; currently tracks Triton 3.8 / PyTorch 2.14): https://github.com/triton-lang/triton-windows

woct0rdho/SageAttention issue #102 (Turing user asking whether triton-windows above 3.2 supports Turing; closed without visible resolution - evidence of stranded demand): https://github.com/woct0rdho/SageAttention/issues/102
ComfyUI-GGUF issue #311 (pytorch 2.7.1 with triton 3.2/triton-windows - the torch/Inductor-vs-triton version-pairing failure class): https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF/issues/311

triton issue #189 (2021-08-05, still open: mma.884 half-rate on Turing, cuBLAS ~46.5 vs Triton ~24.0 TFLOP/s) and issues #6698/#7585 (3.3.x f16-conversion LLVM crash on cc<8.0, fixed 2025-07-22, carried from 3.4) - via this run's sibling items gdn-linear-attention-sm75 and turing-engine-upstream-drift
SGLang issue #7467 (T4 crash on triton 3.3.x; triton==3.2.0 downgrade as the community workaround - the pin in the wild): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/7467

weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive README (vLLM 0.21.0 + torch 2.11.0 base = triton 3.6 FMA tolerated; compute-bound paths are CUDA: FlashQLA/FlashInfer prefill, Marlin weights, own SM70/75 GDN kernel - the production proof of the CUDA-substitution escape): https://github.com/weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive

tile-ai/tilelang releases v0.1.9-v0.1.14 (2026-04-22 SM75 T.gemm fix; 2026-05-25 native SM75 MMA GEMM FP16/INT8/INT4; 2026-07-08 f16-acc/UINT8 dispatchers; 2026-08-03 FMA fallback; 2026-09-02 latest) - the Triton-class substrate that kept Turing MMA: https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/releases

Host records anchoring this item: research/lacunae/outline.yaml (ecosystem-strategy: triton-fma-floor-sm75, the 'dependency deadlock' wording), plan/0006-cu-sm80-on-sm75/README.md ('Triton's tl.dot lost tensor cores below sm80 in Triton 3.3'), plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md execution record ('Triton's tl.dot falls back to FMA below sm_80, so chunked prefill there is FMA-bound'), and sibling results gdn-linear-attention-sm75.json / moe-kernels-sm75.json / mxfp4-nvfp4-ecosystem.json / mla-triton-portability.json / turing-engine-upstream-drift.json (the five rows deferring to this decision)

uncertain: triton_turing_base_version (fork's upstream base not stated in README/commits; the optional vendored triton_kernels and the fp8-e4m3-below-sm89 commit imply a 3.4+-era base - inference only)
triton_turing_cuda13_compat (source build against the host's CUDA 13.3 toolchain untested; CUDA 12.x fallback assumed available)

triton_turing_dot_scaled_on_sm75 (whether the fork's vendored triton_kernels/tl.dot_scaled actually executes on cc75 with MMA - the 'both features' escape is plausible from the repo layout, not demonstrated)

lane_pin_status (sibling records conflict: mla/mxfp4 items assert the lane pins triton <=3.2 while turing-engine-upstream-drift lists the pin decision as open work; the lane venv's installed triton version not re-verified in this item)

v08_carrier_python_cuda_window (v0.8.5-era torch 2.6.0 wheel constraints vs the host's python/driver 610/CUDA 13.3 stack - whether the pin stack installs cleanly or needs the CUDA 12.x container, unverified)
qwen3next_first_vllm_version (first vLLM release carrying qwen3_next model code - placed after v0.8.x by the 2025-09-11 launch blog, exact tag not checked)

torch_27_triton32_break_specifics (the exact Inductor failure mode when triton 3.2 runs under torch >=2.7 is documented via community reports (ComfyUI-GGUF #311 class) and wheel-metadata conflict, not via an upstream statement)

mma1688_first_version (unchanged from the GDN item: which Triton release first emitted m16n8k8 for cc75 - verified at v3.2.0, earlier boundary unpinned; per-dot shape admission for every FLA/vLLM dot also unverified)
triton_36_37_release_dates (PyPI upload dates for 3.6.0/3.7.x not directly captured - placed via torch pairing dates 2026-03-23 (torch 2.11.0 -> 3.6.0) and 2026-07-08 (torch 2.13.0 -> 3.7.1))
fla_042_on_triton32_runtime (0.4.2 declares no triton floor, but actual kernel-feature compatibility on 3.2 silicon is untested until the probe runs)
